title: Lawmakers, groups slam November 15 arrests: Where is maximum tolerance?
summary: 'Where is the maximum tolerance expected of police officers and their respect for freedom of speech and expression in these arrests?' asks Mamamayang Liberal Representative Leila de Lima

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Several personalities and groups raised concerns over the massive arrests of activists and media workers during Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Pax Silica-related protests in Metro Manila on Sunday, November 15.

Progressive group Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (BAYAN) condemned the arrests, saying that they contradict the statement of Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Police General Jose Nartatez Jr.’s claim that the summit’s opening was “generally peaceful.”

“It is the police who were caught on camera kicking down arrested protesters in Manila, manhandling Lakbayan delegates in Sucat, and torturing the detainees by threatening to handcuff those who refuse to have their mugshots taken. They acted like criminal thugs who ordered the throwing of human waste at the Liwasang Bonifacio to discourage people from gathering in the park,” BAYAN said on Monday, November 16.
“The police should also explain the use of deadly weapons such as nails and ice picks in puncturing the tires of the truck to be used for the protest in Manila,” the group added.
As of Sunday, the Manila Police District said at least 11 protesters were arrested by the police in Liwasang Bonifacio.

Most of the arrests in Metro Manila happened in Muntinlupa, where PNP nabbed 276 individuals. They were from Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan, who were heading to Liwasang Bonifacio to join other groups that protested against Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump’s expected arrival.
Some student journalists were also among those arrested.

Mamamayang Liberal Representative Leila de Lima questioned the PNP’s supposed observance of maximum tolerance and respect for freedom of expression. She called for an investigation into the reported violence and alleged denial of detainees’ access to lawyers and family members.
“Where is the maximum tolerance expected of police officers and their respect for freedom of speech and expression in these arrests?” said De Lima.

“We strongly condemn these arrests and the disregard for protesters’ rights. We demand a thorough investigation into the reported unlawful acts committed by the arresting officers and that those responsible be held accountable. All protesters who have been illegally detained must be released immediately!” she added.
On Sunday, several progressive groups gathered outside Camp Bagong Diwa, Taguig City, to denounce the arrests.

“Pinapakita ng pag-aresto sa humigit-kumulang tatlong daang Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan kung kaninong interes ba talaga nagsisilbi ang rehimeng US-Marcos. Sa pagbisita ni Trump, pinapakita talaga na nasa interes ng mga dayuhang bansa ang interes nila,” human rights advocate Charm Maranan said.

(The arrest of almost 300 people of Lakbayani ng Timog Katagulan shows where the interest of the US-Marcos regime truly lies. With Trump’s visit, it just shows that their interest lies in a foreign country.)
The Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan protest march kicked off in Los Baños, Laguna, on November 12, with progressive groups led by BAYAN Timog Katagalugan.

Throughout the march, activist groups and alternative media outlets reported multiple instances of harassment from the police. This included blocking the march’s path, allegedly sabotaging the protest vehicles’ tires, alleged violent manhandling of arrested protesters, and denial of the Commission on Human Rights and lawyers’ entry to police stations.

“Malinaw na ginagarantiya ng Saligang Batas ang kalayaan nating magpahayag at mapayapang magtipon. Ang kakayahan ng mamamayang pumuna at manawagan ng pagbabago ang patunay na buhay ang ating demokrasya,” said Akbayan Representative Chel Diokno.

(It’s clear that the Constitution guarantees our freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. The ability of the citizens to redress their grievances and call for change is proof that our democracy is alive.)

Meanwhile, the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) demanded the immediate release of individuals detained for participating in or covering the protests. The group also appealed to fellow lawyers to provide legal assistance to those arrested, calling on them to “help secure the freedom of the arrestees.”

“While we have already dispatched quick reaction teams to assist the detainees, we need more lawyers to assist them. And we are calling [on] our people’s lawyers to once again rise to the occasion. Our brave clients need brave lawyers,” said NUPL president Ephraim Cortez.
Karapatan secretary general Cristina Palabay also pushed for accountability from police personnel and officers involved in the reported assaults.
“Protestors must be immediately released,” Palabay asserted, urging authorities to guarantee the arrested’s access to legal counsel, relatives, and medical assistance while in custody.

On a similar note, the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines also pressed authorities to stop the violence against media workers, noting the importance of peaceful assembly and press freedom.

“Journalists must be allowed to exercise their duty to cover public events, document abuses, and report the stories of those who take to the streets,” the union stated. – Ren Enano and Rhen Peñada/Rappler.com

Rena Eñano and Rhen Peñada are Rappler volunteers. Eñano is a senior literature student from Ateneo de Manila University, while Peñada is a third-year information technology student from Polytechnic University of the Philippines Sta. Rosa, Laguna Campus.
